blurb: Large shaggy English herding dog with hair over its eyes and a bear-like rolling gait
description: The Old English Sheepdog is a large English herding breed with a long, shaggy grey and white double coat covering its face, and a bear-like rolling gait.
answer: The Old English Sheepdog, often called the Bobtail, is a large herding breed that emerged in England from early pastoral dogs. It typically stands about 56 to 61 cm or more at the withers, with a compact body and a long, shaggy coat that covers the face and eyes. It is widely known as the Dulux dog from paint advertising.

body: The breed comes from the pastoral dogs of England. A bobtailed drover's dog of the early 19th century, the Smithfield or Cotswold Cur, may have been an ancestor, and most fanciers agree the Bearded Collie was part of the original stock. First called the Shepherd's Dog, it was first exhibited in Birmingham in 1873 with only three entries. It soon became a popular show dog, was exported to the United States in the 1880s, and was favored by wealthy American families around 1900. It has been the Dulux paint mascot since 1961.

The Old English Sheepdog has a short, compact body with a deep chest, stands lower at the shoulder than at the loin and moves with a bear-like roll from the rear. The double coat may be any shade of grey, grizzle, black, blue or blue merle, with optional white markings, over a water-resistant undercoat. Puppies are born black and white. The tail was traditionally docked, giving the Bobtail name, but tailed dogs are now common where docking is banned.

The available sources say little about the breed's temperament. Herding instinct and trainability can be assessed at herding tests, and dogs with basic herding instinct can be trained for herding trials.

The long, thick coat is said to shed only when brushed, and show dogs have been elaborately groomed since at least 1907. The breed competes in agility, obedience, rally, flyball, tracking and herding events, and as a large herding dog it is generally expected to need regular activity.

Conditions reported in the breed include hip dysplasia, gastric dilatation volvulus (bloat), allergic skin disease, demodicosis, dilated cardiomyopathy and the MDR1 mutation, which increases sensitivity to certain drugs. One North American study found hip dysplasia in 11.1 percent of dogs examined. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.1 years.

faq.a: The breed is described as shedding only when brushed, but the long, thick double coat needs substantial grooming.

faq.q: How long do Old English Sheepdogs live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.1 years for the breed.

faq.q: Why is the Old English Sheepdog called a Bobtail?
faq.a: The nickname comes from the tradition of docking the breed's tail. Many countries now ban cosmetic docking, so tailed dogs are increasingly common.

faq.q: Is the Old English Sheepdog recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 16 in Group 1.
